description: Kneeling in the straw to rub a damp newborn dry with a fistful of clean straw, working along its back the wrong way on purpose.
Setting two wet lambs down in a crate under the lamp and folding a sack over half the top to hold the warmth in.
Steering a new lamb's nose the last inch to the udder with one careful finger, then sitting back on both heels to watch it find the rest itself.
Cupping a damp lamb's whole chin in both palms and tipping its muzzle up until it stops shaking and starts blinking properly.
Pressing a damp newborn against the chest and swaying slightly, feeling it wriggle its back legs against the forearms for the first time.
Folding both knees under to sit flat in the straw beside two lambs that are still deciding whether their own legs are reliable yet.
Holding a bottle out at arm's length while a lamb drives its whole body into it, both feet leaving the straw on impact.
Warming a bottle by pressing it hard against the side of the neck and tilting the head over it to check the temperature.
Kneeling with two bottles going at once, one in each fist, while a third lamb shoves its head between both arms looking for a third teat that does not exist.
Tipping a bottle almost vertical to keep the teat full, free arm braced against the hurdle rail as two lambs compete for the same angle.
Wedging a bottle between the knees to free both hands for a moment, only for a lamb to claim it immediately and refuse to let go.
Walking backwards through a gateway with a lamb held low in each arm, the ewe tracking nose to heel the whole length of the passage.
Lifting a hurdle clear of the mud with one knee under its bottom rail and a shoulder under its middle, swinging it wide in one move.
Carrying a whole bale pressed flat against the chest, chin resting on top, navigating a gate latch by feel alone.
Shaking a bucket once sharply so the whole flock swings its heads around at the same moment like a single hinge.
Dragging a spare hurdle backwards across the shed floor with both heels dug in, steering it around a corner with a hip.
Swinging the field gate wide and stepping well back out of the rush, one hand still resting on the top bar as the mob pours through.
Crouching in the wet grass with both forearms across both knees, watching the mob spread out and counting them off by which way the heads are pointing.
Walking the full length of the wall line slowly, touching each stone post with a knuckle to pace the count without losing it.
Sitting on the very top of the gate, both feet hooked on the second bar, watching the first lambs hit full speed across the open field.
Forking clean straw into a pen and then treading it flat with both feet, bouncing slightly to get an even bed before the ewe is moved in.
Leaning right over the top rail on both elbows to count the pen a second time because the first answer came out wrong and counting again to see if it comes out differently.
Setting a kettle on the shelf over the water pipe, turning back to the pen, and promptly forgetting the kettle exists.
Dozing sitting up in a wooden chair beside the pen, chin dropped, with a lamb curled right across one foot and using it as a pillow.
Jerking awake in the chair with both eyes open, counting the lambs against the ewe's flank before the brain has caught up with the body.
